body:
Of course it works!
I set the option:
`$SmartRoot = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "SMART"`
and it was ok.

The problem, IMHO. is that the comment was not clear enough, 
In fact it is written:

```
# SMART location
# If SMART.exe exists directly under this directory, it will be used.
# Otherwise, the script will search versioned SMART-*-win64-portable subdirectories (default portable layout).
$SmartRoot = $env:LOCALAPPDATA
```

I should have written an example, to explain this better. 
Something like:

```
# SMART location
# The script will search versioned SMART-*-win64-portable subdirectories (default portable layout),
# unless SMART.exe exists under a directory with a different name in the user LOCALAPPDATA.
# In this case, change the line of code below, from:
# $SmartRoot = $env:LOCALAPPDATA
# to:
# $SmartRoot = $env:LOCALAPPDATA "DIRNAME"
# For example, in case of a path like this:
# C:\users\username\AppData\Local\SMART
# write:
# $SmartRoot = $env:LOCALAPPDATA "SMART"
```
But, of course it is up to you!

Regards,
Topoldo
